id: title:DanielVisca:serve text embedding 3 small at 256 dimensions

observations.behavior: Adds a new enum variant OpenAITextEmbeddingSmall256 with the serialized name text-embedding-3-small-256.
observations.posthog_connection: This could allow PostHog to request embeddings at 256 dimensions from OpenAI for high-volume documents.

observations.behavior: Updates request body construction to include an optional dimensions field, populated only when requested by the model. This is also guarded by tests in P1.F1.H9.
observations.posthog_connection: Allows downstream embedding workers or API clients to explicitly pass the dimensions parameter to OpenAI's endpoint.

observations.behavior: Adds unit tests asserting that the Small256 variant includes dimensions=256 and does not send this field for other variants; also checks round-trip serialization and shared rate-limit bucketing.
observations.posthog_connection: Provides regression protection against incorrect dimension handling and ensures compatibility with existing limit-bucketing behavior.

observations.limitations: All hunks are contained within rust/common/types/src/embeddings.rs and its immediate callers; no changes were observed to configuration, migration, deployment, billing, or end-user-facing documentation. The tier depends on whether this capability reaches a broader system boundary (e.g., warehouse ingestion, managed warehouse, or desktop app) rather than remaining isolated to type definitions and worker helpers.

review.limitations: All hunks are contained within rust/common/types/src/embeddings.rs and its immediate callers; no changes were observed to configuration, migration, deployment, billing, or end-user-facing documentation. The tier depends on whether this capability reaches a broader system boundary (e.g., warehouse ingestion, managed warehouse, or desktop app) rather than remaining isolated to type definitions and worker helpers.
review.reason: This chunk adds a bounded new capability—supporting 256-dimension embeddings via OpenAI—and demonstrates implementation and relevant checks: updated request construction, matching response parsing, shared limits key, input-window preservation, truncation guard, and several targeted unit assertions. It is substantive but remains localized without demonstrated systemic reach across components.
review.posthog_relevance: Could enable PostHog customers who use OpenAI's text-embedding-3-small at reduced dimensions, potentially supporting high-volume document workflows while sharing the same model name and rate-limit bucket as the standard small embedding.
review.uncertainty: The actual benefit depends on adoption and integration points not shown here; this could remain an internal-only feature if downstream consumers do not adopt it.
